clue.text: Composer responsible for Hair?

definitions.meaning: Samuel ... was an American composer, best known for his Adagio for Strings
a man who cuts hair for a living; the capital H dresses it as the musical Hair

explanation.surface: A question about who wrote the music for the stage show Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Hair?' suggests the 1960s musical, so 'Composer' seems to be asking for its writer; really the second half is just a hairdresser.
explanation.definitionFit: Barber is the surname of a twentieth-century American composer, and a barber is a men's hairdresser.

clue.text: Terribly eager to correspond

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is very keen to keep up letter-writing with a pen friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that agree correspond with each other, matching or tallying.

clue.text: Fellow, English dandy, looks promising

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or fellow
a swell is a fashionably dressed man, a dandy

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed Englishman cuts a promising figure.
explanation.walkthrough: BOD is British slang for a chap or person.
explanation.definitionFit: If something bodes well it is a promising sign, an omen of good things.

clue.text: Feel bitter about inmate losing identity

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away

parts.note: an inmate is a resident, of a house or institution
ID is the usual short form of identity

explanation.surface: A prisoner is resentful at being stripped of who he is.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter or aggrieved about it.

clue.text: Display feathers in confrontation

parts.note: to display something is to show it
down is the soft fine feathering of birds

explanation.surface: A bird puffs out its plumage during a stand-off with a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive final confrontation between rivals is a showdown, as in a Western gunfight.

clue.text: Son and father meet in hotels to order some food

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A father and son get together in hotels to order a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to order' shuffles MEET IN HOTELS into NISHOMELETTE. 'Order' looks like asking for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish omelette, made with potato and onion, is a dish of food.

clue.text: Usual charge for arms

definitions.meaning: in heraldry a charge is a design on a shield, and one of the simple basic designs has this name

explanation.surface: The standard fee for weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' here is a coat of arms, and a 'charge' is a figure placed on the shield, not a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary means usual, and in heraldry an ordinary is a simple geometric charge like a bend or chevron.

clue.text: Opera singer needs new bed

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer

explanation.surface: A soprano demands a new bed in her dressing room.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan is a type of bed with a thick base and no headboard or footboard.

clue.text: Could be European bird diving into river

indicators.note: a bird diving into something ends up inside it

parts.note: the Weser is a river in north-west Germany
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Perhaps a European bird is plunging into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A Westerner, someone from the West, could be a European, hence the hedge 'Could be'.

clue.text: Book journeys, obliged to announce one's holding up train perhaps

parts.note: rides are journeys, on horseback or by vehicle

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: obliged, as in forced to do something, means made

explanation.surface: Someone books trips and feels compelled to make an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: MADE said aloud gives MAID. The 'train' is a bride's dress train, not a railway one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid attending a bride may hold up the long train of her wedding dress, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Old striker's short of a garment

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a vesta is an old-fashioned match, something struck to light it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A retired footballer lacks a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of a' removes A from VESTA. 'Striker' suggests football or industrial action; here it is a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest is a garment worn under a shirt (in American usage, a waistcoat).

clue.text: For a start, high priest is about to invest capital

indicators.note: for a start points to the opening letter of the following word
the priest is about, that is around, the next piece

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel, a crossword regular
to sink money into something is to invest it

explanation.surface: To begin with, a senior cleric is set to put money into a capital fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High priest' looks like one phrase, but the two words do separate jobs; 'is about' means the priest's name goes round the word for investing.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Prepared bread rolls and port

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: prepared, as in ready, means set
nan, or naan, is Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: Someone has baked bread rolls and has a glass of port with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' turns the whole of SETNAN backwards. It looks like baked rolls, and 'port' looks like the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a port city on the Loire in western France.

clue.text: Odd bits of gauze applied after a nasty illness?

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other in the answer
the odd-numbered letters of the word, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A dressing of gauze put on after a bad sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: The first, third and fifth letters of 'gauze' give GUE, which goes after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is a fever with fits of shivering, especially malaria; the question mark hedges a generic description.

clue.text: Change of tone as university pulls out of degree ceremony

indicators.note: pulling out of something means leaving it, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a graduation is the ceremony where degrees are conferred

explanation.surface: The mood shifts when a university withdraws from its degree day.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradation is a gradual change, as from one shade or tone to another.

clue.text: Endlessly bad luck, but uncompromising

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: hard lines is a British expression of sympathy meaning bad luck

explanation.surface: Someone suffers constant misfortune yet refuses to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD LINES is a British phrase meaning 'bad luck'; drop its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardline stance is unyielding and refuses to compromise.

clue.text: Bell, if set to go off, rings in an emergency?

indicators.note: going off suggests something exploding or going wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An alarm bell set to ring when there is an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' looks like a bell ringing; it is the ring-shaped floats thrown to someone drowning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifebelts are ring-shaped buoyancy aids thrown to people in the water in an emergency.

clue.text: Wealthy person and former sweetheart count, perhaps

parts.note: nob is British slang for a rich or upper-class person
leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A rich man and an ex-girlfriend tot up figures, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a verb; it is the aristocratic title. 'former' marks LEMAN as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is a European aristocrat, one example of a nobleman.

clue.text: Brush round everyone in dance hall

indicators.note: the brush goes round, enclosing the next piece

parts.note: a broom is a long-handled brush
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Someone sweeps around all the people in a dance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom is a large hall or room used for dancing.

clue.text: Announce just what the commuter will pay

indicators.note: announcing means speaking aloud, so a word that sounds alike is wanted

parts.note: just, meaning even-handed, is fair

explanation.surface: A call to declare fairly what a commuter must pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fare is the price a passenger pays for a journey.

clue.text: Getting into argument, petty officer's given warning

indicators.note: the petty officer gets into, so goes inside, the argument

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
PO is the abbreviation for petty officer

explanation.surface: A naval officer caught up in a row is given a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is a private warning or piece of advance information.

clue.text: Enough to make little Sarah a shoe

definitions.text: Enough to make little Sarah a shoe

parts.words: Enough to make little Sarah a shoe
parts.note: Sal, the pet name for Sarah, needs only a small joining word put inside her to become a piece of open footwear

explanation.surface: Someone has just enough money to buy little Sarah a pair of shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: SAL is short for Sarah; putting AND inside it makes SANDAL. No clue word gives AND, so this is a cryptic hint, not ordinary wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal is a light open shoe held on by straps.

clue.text: Tendency to move about aimlessly

definitions.meaning: the ... of something is its general tendency or direction
to wander about with no purpose

explanation.surface: An inclination to wander around without direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Drift is a general tendency, as of an argument, and to drift is to wander aimlessly.

clue.text: Relaxed, having two-way bet?

definitions.meaning: in betting you can lay a horse (bet against it) or back it (bet for it), so doing both is having laid and backed

explanation.surface: A gambler stays calm after hedging a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: Betting both ways means laying a horse and backing it; the hyphenated phrase shows both.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone laid-back is relaxed and easy-going.

clue.text: Appearance at start of evening class

parts.note: the cast of someone's face is its look or appearance

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Turning up at the beginning of an evening class.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in Hindu society.

clue.text: Once fashionable skirt makes some reminisce

indicators.note: some of the following word is taken, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Thinking back on an old-style short skirt brings back memories.
explanation.definitionFit: The miniskirt, or mini, was the height of fashion in the 1960s.

clue.text: Still a situation in which debate is impossible?

definitions.meaning: still means not moving at all

definitions.text: a situation in which debate is impossible?
definitions.meaning: a debate needs a motion to argue over, so without one there can be none

explanation.surface: A deadlock where no discussion can take place.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'motion-less': a formal debate needs a motion put before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless is perfectly still, not moving in any way.

clue.text: Case put in position

parts.note: a stance is a position, physical or on an issue

explanation.surface: A box placed in its proper spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case or example of something.

clue.text: One unlikely to eat seconds after cooking

indicators.note: cooking means altering, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who is not likely to want a second helping once the meal is cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' shuffles S and AFTER together. 'Seconds' suggests second helpings at a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A faster is a person who goes without food, so they are unlikely to eat.
